title: O Son of God, on Thee We Call
description: O Son of God, on Thee We Call in Tonic Solfa to HOLY MATRIMONY, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: John Brownlie translated these words from the Greek service books for Hymns from the Greek Office Books (Paisley, 1904).
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Common Particular Metre (8.8.6.8.8.6), and this page sets them to HOLY MATRIMONY; any other Common Particular Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O Son of God, on Thee we call, Blest Je-su, ere the dark-ness fall, Come near us in Thy grace; We own the sins that mar our life, And stem our ef-forts in the strife, And shamed we hide our face.

lines: O Son of God, on Thee we call,
Blest Jesu, ere the darkness fall,
Come near us in Thy grace;
We own the sins that mar our life,
And stem our efforts in the strife,
And shamed we hide our face.
The morning came, and hope was clear,
And void the soul of doubt and fear;
But ere the noontide shone,
The light was darkened in the sky,
For thickest clouds came rolling nigh,
And all our peace was gone.
And now the night is bringing dread,
For guilt is resting on our head; —
O Christ, our prayers hear,
Who bore our sorrows on the Cross,
Who paid for us our priceless loss, —
And come in mercy near.
Give us to know Thy strength is given
To all who tread the path to heaven —
That we may fail to gain,
And fall to rise, and forward press
In light and dark, in storm and stress
Of fear and doubt and pain.
Give us to know Thy mercies wait
On those who knock at heaven's gate,
That none can knock in vain;
For He who died for sinful men
Would have them come, and come again,
Nor fainting e'er refrain.

source: John Brownlie, Hymns from the Greek Office Books (1904)
licence: Public domain: John Brownlie died in 1925.
credits: Translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925) from the Greek, public domain, as printed in Hymns from the Greek Office Books; set to HOLY MATRIMONY by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
